headline: South Korea's main stock index fell 3.65% on Monday as chip stocks slid, even after Samsung Electronics reported record earnings.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: the full Korea Times report with exchange figures was read; it is a one-day move and analysts disagree on the cause, but the fall is the largest in six weeks.
importance_line: What changed is that South Korea's AI-linked stock market had its sharpest one-day fall in six weeks despite record chip earnings, which matters first to savers and pension holders with Korean or Asian shares in their funds, then to foreign investors and the chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, and the doubt is that analysts disagree on the cause and one cautions that the fall does not mean Korean chipmakers are losing competitiveness.
summary: The Korea Times reports that South Korea's main share index, the KOSPI, fell 3.65% to 6,384.24 on Monday 12 Oct 2026, its biggest one-day drop since 2 Sep and a fourth straight losing day, as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, the two big memory-chip makers, lost about 4.4% and 4.5% amid steady selling by foreign investors. This continues the slump Bloomberg described in our 11 Oct 2026 edition: the index fell even though Samsung reported record results last Thursday, and an analyst links the fall to renewed AI bubble worries, while the Korea Times notes that the OpenAI revenue reports behind those worries reflected different accounting methods, not lower sales.
